correctness.rationale: The six primitive rays are permutations of (-A,B,A-B) (three rays only at the coprime endpoint (2,1)). For A<2B, each facet cone is generated by the two explicit integer vectors in RESULT.md. Their positive determinants are m_-=A(2B-A) and m_+=B(2A-B). The Bezout basis gives q=-p mod m, hence both quotient weights and exact cyclic group orders. Unimodular coordinates give 1/3(1,2) at (2,1). Coprimality makes (1,1) the unique smooth pair. The HJ continued fraction of m/q then determines the full resolution chains. Independently checked all 1967 coprime pairs with B<=80, including all six facet determinants, q-coprimality and edge counts; this finite test supplements, not replaces, the symbolic proof.
residual_risks: The quotient-weight convention depends on orientation; verified sign via p in the unimodular basis and (3,2) and (2,1) examples.
The original Wu fan definition and alpha formula were accessible in the submitted frozen proof and indexed abstract/synopsis, not full preprint text.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality of the full parameterized cyclic quotient types and HJ baskets survives. Wu realizes all alpha values and studies coarse singularity conditions; Liu–Zhu and the published local class-group computation determine the (A,B)=(3,2) orders 3 and 8 but not q types nor all coprime B<=A<=2B. The standard toric quotient algorithm computes types from a given cone but does not already evaluate this family. Full Wu paper access was unavailable, so undiscovered Section 5 coverage remains a specific risk.
residual_risks: Preprint full text of highly relevant Wu paper unavailable; best-of-knowledge O carries that specific coverage risk.

value.rationale: Classifies a genuine local-geometric invariant for a natural two-parameter K-polystable toric surface realization family, including both endpoints, all minimal resolution chains, and unbounded quotient orders as alpha tends to 1/2. These are finer than existing global alpha or yes/no Q-factorial data and useful for local birational geometry.
residual_risks: Interpretation restricted to the defined toric surface family.

scientific_limitations: The result treats n=2 and the face-fan surface only, not higher-dimensional cones.
